# A later chapter whose filename has a space

This chapter marks a term, [Late]{.index}, and carries a marker of its own —
which must be refused, because the first chapter in book order already has one.

The contested term again, sorted differently here. The first chapter in book
order wins, and this one is reported: [Contested]{.index sort="Zzz"}.

Marked a second time, with the same key this chapter already wrote. The clash
with the first chapter is one thing for the author to fix, not one per mark,
so the report must still fire exactly once: [Contested]{.index sort="Zzz"}.

A cross-reference whose target no chapter of this book marks at all. Counted
across the whole render, it must be reported exactly once — which only holds
if a single chapter draws the report: [missing]{.index
entry="Missing Reference" see="Nowhere At All"}.

::: {.qi-index-here}
:::

A range opening that also carries a cross-reference, which takes the locator's
place — so the range is refused here, and the closing in the chapter after this
one must NOT be paired with it. Were it paired, that closing's locator would be
suppressed on the strength of an opening this chapter had already refused, and
the entry would print its cross-reference with no locator at all:
[Spanned]{.index range="open" see="Late"}.
